summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML directly where data lives, offering in-database model training, inference, embedding generation, and LLM access without moving data to external systems. A major trend is native vector search for GenAI retrieval (RAG), with analysts projecting that by 2026 roughly 30% of enterprises will rely on vector-based retrieval and up to 75% of enterprise AI apps will depend on vector search. Platforms differ sharply in whether vector search is natively built-in versus provided through extensions, and in how deeply managed LLMs (e.g., Snowflake Cortex, Vertex AI) are integrated.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, embeddings)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs and embedding models via SQL/Python functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER, EMBED_TEXT). Cortex Search offers managed hybrid retrieval, Cortex Analyst enables natural-language-to-SQL, and the newer Snowflake Postgres brings Cortex-powered AI directly to Postgres applications while data stays in Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with built-in vector distance functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE, VECTOR_INNER_PRODUCT) and managed Cortex Search for retrieval; no third-party extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Deep native integration with Snowflake-hosted and partner LLMs (e.g., models from Anthropic, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) accessible directly through SQL and Python without managing AI infrastructure.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing billed in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM/embedding functions are charged per token processed plus underlying warehouse/compute costs. Cortex Search and serverless features incur separate serverless credit consumption.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration (generative AI, embeddings, remote models)
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, etc.) using SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call hosted foundation models (Gemini) via ML.GENERATE_TEXT, generate embeddings with ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and run AI tasks like translation and sentiment directly in SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides built-in VECTOR_SEARCH functionality with vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) and the ML.DISTANCE/VECTOR_SEARCH functions for similarity search over embeddings stored in BigQuery tables.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Vertex AI, enabling remote/connection models to call Gemini and other foundation models plus embedding models directly from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed via BigQuery compute (on-demand per-TB scanned or capacity slots) plus Vertex AI charges for calls to hosted generative/embedding models; vector indexing and storage incur standard storage costs.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database LLM/embedding workflows
databases.description: PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds a vector data type and similarity operators with HNSW and IVFFlat indexing, while pgai (from Timescale) enables calling LLM and embedding providers (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) and automating embedding pipelines from within SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Extension-based, not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search requires installing the pgvector extension; core Postgres has no built-in vector type or similarity search. pgvector provides HNSW/IVFFlat indexes once enabled.
databases.llm_integration: Via extensions such as pgai and pgvectorscale, which let Postgres call external LLM/embedding APIs and manage embeddings; no built-in LLM in core Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: PostgreSQL and pgvector/pgai are open source and free to use; costs come from hosting/compute (self-managed or via a managed provider) plus any external LLM/embedding API usage fees.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL integration with SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using SQL by invoking Amazon SageMaker endpoints, Amazon Bedrock foundation models, and Amazon Comprehend for NLP, without moving data out of the database or requiring ML expertise in the data layer.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Aurora ML itself does not provide vector search; on Aurora PostgreSQL, vector search is available only through the pgvector extension, so it is extension-based rather than a built-in Aurora ML capability.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models through SQL functions, enabling generative AI and custom-model inference from Aurora.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage/IO costs plus the usage costs of the invoked SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend services.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (in-warehouse model training and inference via SQL with SageMaker/Bedrock)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables users to create, train, and deploy ML models using familiar SQL CREATE MODEL statements, leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot under the hood. It also supports bring-your-own-model inference and integration with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI directly from the data warehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not a core Redshift ML feature. Redshift ML focuses on predictive modeling; vector similarity is handled separately in Redshift (e.g., via vector data type/functions for embeddings), and is not part of the Redshift ML service itself.
databases.llm_integration: Supports calling Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted LLMs from SQL for generative AI use cases alongside traditional supervised models.
databases.pricing_notes: Model training uses SageMaker and is billed by SageMaker usage; prediction functions run in the Redshift cluster. You pay standard Redshift compute/storage plus SageMaker/Bedrock charges for training and external inference.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model serving, fine-tuning, agents) with Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides tools to build, fine-tune, serve, and evaluate ML and generative AI models, including foundation model APIs, agent frameworks, and MLflow-based lifecycle management. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database tightly integrated with Unity Catalog and Delta tables for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, fully managed vector database that automatically syncs embeddings from Delta tables and supports similarity queries within the Databricks platform.
databases.llm_integration: Deep native integration via Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs (hosting open and proprietary LLMs like Llama, DBRX, and external providers), plus agent and fine-tuning tooling.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute, model serving, and Vector Search endpoints; foundation model usage billed per token or per endpoint, in addition to cloud infrastructure costs.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search (native vector indexing and semantic search within MongoDB)
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run semantic/similarity queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage. It supports hybrid search combining vector, full-text, and metadata filtering for RAG and AI-powered applications on operational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is built into MongoDB Atlas with native vector indexes and the $vectorSearch operator (ANN via HNSW), requiring no external vector database or third-party extension.
databases.llm_integration: No built-in hosted LLM, but tight integrations and reference frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, OpenAI) let developers generate and store embeddings and build RAG pipelines on Atlas.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas; vector search runs on Atlas Search nodes with cluster-based pricing, so costs scale with cluster tier/dedicated Search node resources. External embedding/LLM API usage is billed separately by the provider.
